election.name: November 5, 2024 general election
election.summary: Lakewood voters chose a president, their member of Congress (CD-7), a CU regent, state representatives and two Jefferson County commissioners, and voted on 14 statewide measures. Locally, voters approved Lakewood Ballot Issue 2A, which lets the city keep revenue above its TABOR limit permanently, along with Jefferson County 1A and RTD 7A, which made similar changes for the county and RTD.
election.turnout: Jefferson County: 367,408 ballots from 437,432 active voters (about 84%). Lakewood (Ballot Issue 2A contest): 89,396 ballots from 111,507 registered voters (80.2%). Statewide: 3,240,549 ballots (79.5% of active voters).

measures.short_title: Keep revenue above TABOR limits permanently
measures.summary: Let the city keep and spend all revenue above its TABOR limit starting in 2026, with no new or higher tax. The extra money is split equally among parks, recreation and open space; public safety; and streets, sidewalks, paths and infrastructure, and kept in a separate account. A 2017 voter approval to keep this revenue was set to expire in 2025. Jefferson County count: 89,396 ballots cast of 111,507 registered Lakewood voters.

measures.short_title: County keeps revenue above TABOR limits
measures.summary: Let Jefferson County keep and spend all revenue from its existing sources starting in fiscal year 2024, without raising any tax or mill levy. The money goes to roads, bridges and other infrastructure and to public safety, including wildfire and flood work and mental health and addiction programs, with yearly review by an independent auditor and a citizen committee.

measures.short_title: RTD keeps revenue above TABOR limits
measures.summary: Permanently exempt RTD from TABOR revenue and spending limits so it can keep revenue it would otherwise refund. Yes/No counts are Jefferson County totals; district-wide totals were not collected.
Extend the veterans' property tax exemption to veterans with individual unemployability status. Constitutional amendment; needed 55% statewide. Statewide: 2,212,022 yes, 812,638 no.
Create an independent board to decide judicial discipline cases. Constitutional amendment; needed 55% statewide. Statewide: 2,150,820 yes, 793,642 no.
Allow courts to deny bail for first-degree murder when proof is evident or the presumption is great. Constitutional amendment; needed 55% statewide. Statewide: 2,058,063 yes, 953,652 no.
Remove the constitutional language defining marriage as only between one man and one woman. Constitutional amendment; needed 55% statewide. Statewide: 1,982,200 yes, 1,099,228 no.
Move up deadlines for filing initiative and referendum petitions and for judicial retention notices. Constitutional amendment; needed 55% statewide. Statewide: 1,293,879 yes, 1,591,312 no.
Add a right to abortion to the state constitution and remove the ban on using public funds for abortion. Constitutional amendment; needed 55% statewide. Statewide: 1,921,593 yes, 1,179,261 no.
Add a right to K-12 school choice to the state constitution. Constitutional amendment; needed 55% statewide. It received less than 50% statewide. Statewide: 1,507,236 yes, 1,548,679 no.
Let the state keep all sports betting tax revenue above $29 million a year, rather than refund it. Statewide: 2,340,370 yes, 721,237 no.
Add a 6.5% excise tax on sales of firearms and ammunition, with the money going to designated programs. Statewide: 1,675,123 yes, 1,406,112 no.

Create a state Peace Officer Training and Support Fund. Statewide: 1,583,118 yes, 1,415,528 no.
Replace party primaries for certain offices with one all-candidate primary, with the top four advancing to a ranked-choice general election. Statewide: 1,385,060 yes, 1,595,256 no.

facts.text: Jefferson County counted 367,408 ballots from 437,432 active voters (about 84%): 342,033 by mail and 25,363 in person. The county canvass certified the results on Nov. 27, 2024.
In the Lakewood Ballot Issue 2A contest, 89,396 ballots were counted from 111,507 registered Lakewood voters (80.2%).
Statewide, 3,240,549 of 4,074,680 active voters cast ballots (79.5%); 92.2% voted by mail. The Secretary of State certified the statewide results on Dec. 6, 2024.
No state Senate race covering Lakewood (Senate Districts 20 and 22) was on the 2024 ballot; the only Jefferson County senate contests were Districts 16, 19 and 26.
Lakewood voters had no State Board of Education race in 2024. The only board race on Jefferson County ballots was for Congressional District 2, which does not include Lakewood.
The certified county report lists no Jeffco Public Schools ballot measure in November 2024.

Colorado voters decided 14 statewide measures in 2024: seven constitutional amendments (G, H, I, J, K, 79, 80) and seven statutory propositions (JJ, KK, 127, 128, 129, 130, 131). Amendments needed 55% to pass.
Every judge on the Jefferson County ballot received a majority 'yes' vote in Jefferson County.

open_questions: Lakewood-only vote counts (by precinct) for races other than Ballot Issue 2A were not collected; most figures are Jefferson County totals.

Lakewood 2A result is taken from the certified Jefferson County summary report (copy hosted on morrisonco.us). No City of Lakewood page with the 2024 result was found; jeffco.us results pages could not be fetched.
District-wide totals for RTD Ballot Issue 7A and RTD District D were not collected (only Jefferson County portions).
Statewide figures for president, CD-7, CU regent and measures come from Ballotpedia and Wikipedia; they were not checked line-by-line against the SOS abstract, which could not be fully read.

Party labels are not printed in the Jefferson County summary report; they come from Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, Colorado Community Media and the SOS abstract. Ron Tupa (CD-7) is shown as Unity in Wikipedia's results table but as Independent elsewhere on that page.
Judges' full first names are not in the county report; only surnames are given.

Confirm whether any part of Lakewood falls in House Districts 24 or 25, Senate District 16, or the Foothills Park & Recreation District (Ballot Issue 6D, approved 44,954 to 14,500). Foothills says it serves unincorporated Jefferson County.
The Jeffco report gives 342,033 mail + 25,363 in-person = 367,396 ballots, 12 fewer than the 367,408 in the summary report; the gap is not explained.
